# Using pdm as a Dart Library

`lib/src/*.dart` has no CLI awareness at all — flags, terminal color, and
help text live exclusively under `lib/src/cli/*.dart`. This means the core
download engine is usable as a normal Dart package dependency.

```yaml
# your pubspec.yaml
dependencies:
  pdm:
    git: https://github.com/psdkjoon/pdm.git
```

```dart
import 'package:pdm/pdm.dart';
```

## Quick start

```dart
import 'package:pdm/pdm.dart';

final manager = DownloadManager();
manager.add(
  'https://example.com/file.iso',
  options: const TaskOptions(connections: 8, retries: 5),
  schedule: Schedule(every: Duration(days: 1)),
);

manager.events.listen((record) {
  print('${record.id}: ${record.status.name} (${(record.progress * 100).toStringAsFixed(1)}%)');
});
```

## `DownloadManager`

The core engine — owns the task queue, persistence, and scheduling timer.
This is what both the CLI's `--foreground` mode and the `pdmd` daemon
process wrap.

```dart
DownloadManager({
  TaskStore? store,
  int maxConcurrentTasks = 3,
  String? downloadDir,
  List<DownloadRule> rules = const [],
  Map<String, String> onCompleteAliases = const {},
  bool notifications = false,
  int? globalSpeedLimitBytesPerSec,
  HistoryLog? history,
})
```

| Member | Signature | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `events` | `Stream<TaskRecord>` | Broadcast stream; emits on every state change |
| `tasks` | `List<TaskRecord>` | Snapshot of every known task |
| `get(id)` | `TaskRecord? Function(String)` | Look up one task by id |
| `add(...)` | see below | Queues a new download |
| `start(id)` | `Future<void>` | Re-queues a paused/failed task |
| `pause(id)` | `Future<void>` | Pauses an active or queued task |
| `cancel(id)` | `Future<void>` | Cancels a task and deletes its partial file |
| `remove(id, {deleteFile})` | `Future<void>` | Removes a task's record, optionally deleting the file |
| `dispose()` | `void` | Stops the schedule timer and closes the event stream |

```dart
TaskRecord add(
  String url, {
  String? savePath,
  TaskOptions options = const TaskOptions(),
  bool startPaused = false,
  Schedule? schedule,
  bool allowDuplicate = false,
})
```

Throws `StateError` if a non-duplicate-allowed add matches an existing
non-terminal task's URL or save path.

## `TaskOptions`

Everything about how a single task should be fetched — this is the
programmatic equivalent of every per-task `add` flag documented in
[Commands add](/pdm/commands-add/). See `lib/src/models.dart` for the
complete constructor; every field maps directly to a flag of the same
purpose (`connections`, `headers`, `userAgent`, `referer`, `cookie`,
`cookieFile`, `proxy`, `proxyUser`, `proxyPass`, `proxyBypass`, `retries`,
`retryDelayMs`, `retryBackoff`, `timeoutSeconds`, `speedLimitBytesPerSec`,
`checksumAlgo`, `checksumValue`, `authUser`, `authPass`, `insecure`,
`overwrite`, `priority`, `maxRedirects`, `onComplete`, `checkDiskSpace`).

`TaskOptions` also has `mergeRule(DownloadRule rule)`, which returns a new
`TaskOptions` with the rule's overridable fields applied — this is exactly
what the CLI uses to apply a matching config-file rule before a task
starts.

## `TaskRecord`

The full state of one task, as emitted on `DownloadManager.events` and
returned by `DownloadManager.tasks`/`get()`. This is also the shape you get
back from `pdm list --json`.

| Field | Type |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | `String` |
| `url` | `String` |
| `savePath` | `String` |
| `status` | `DownloadStatus` |
| `totalBytes` | `int?` |
| `supportsRange` | `bool` |
| `options` | `TaskOptions` |
| `segments` | `List<Segment>` |
| `error` | `String?` |
| `createdAt` / `updatedAt` | `DateTime` |
| `startPaused` | `bool` |
| `schedule` | `Schedule?` |

Computed getters: `downloadedBytes` (sum across segments), `progress`
(fraction 0.0–1.0), `connections` (`options.connections`).

## `DownloadStatus`

```dart
enum DownloadStatus {
  queued, scheduled, probing, downloading,
  paused, verifying, completed, failed, canceled,
}
```

See [Task Lifecycle](/pdm/task-lifecycle/) for the full transition diagram.
`statusFromString(String)` parses the `.name` form back into the enum
(falling back to `failed` for an unrecognized string).

## `Schedule`, `Segment`, `DownloadRule`

```dart
class Schedule {
  final DateTime? at;
  final Duration? every;
  final bool onStartup;
}

class Segment {
  final int index, start, end;
  int downloaded;
  // .length, .remaining, .isComplete
}

class DownloadRule {
  final String pattern;
  final String? saveDir;
  final int? connections;
  final String? proxy;
  final int? speedLimitBytesPerSec;
  final Map<String, String> headers;
  final String? onComplete;
  bool matches(String url);   // RegExp(pattern).hasMatch(url)
}
```

## Config helpers (`src/config.dart`)

| Function | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `loadConfig({String? path})` | Loads and parses `PdmConfig` from disk (or built-in defaults if the file is absent) |
| `dumpDefaultConfig({PdataFormat format})` | Renders `PdmConfig.defaults` as a string in the given format |
| `writeDefaultConfig(path, {format, force})` | Writes the rendered default config to disk |
| `defaultConfigPath()` | Resolves the platform-appropriate default config path, honoring `PDM_CONFIG_PATH` |
| `defaultStateDir()` | Resolves the state directory, honoring `XDG_STATE_HOME` |
| `homeDir()` | Cross-platform home directory resolution |
| `expandHome(String path)` | Expands a leading `~` to `homeDir()` |

`PdmConfig` itself mirrors every key in [Configuration
Schema](/pdm/configuration-schema/) as a typed field, with
`PdmConfig.defaults` as a `const` instance of the built-in defaults,
`.toJson()`, and `.fromMap(Map)`.

## Checksums (`src/hashing.dart`)

| Function | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `hashFile(String path, String algo)` | `Future<String>` hex digest; `algo` one of `md5`, `sha1`, `sha256`, `sha512` |
| `verifyFileChecksum(path, algo, expected)` | `Future<bool>`, case-insensitive compare |
| `sha256Hex(List<int> bytes)` | Hash raw bytes directly (used internally for installer payload verification) |

All four algorithms are implemented from scratch on top of `dart:typed_data`
— no `crypto` package dependency anywhere in pdm.

## Hooks and notifications (`src/hooks.dart`)

| Function | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `builtinOnCompleteCommands()` | Returns the platform's map of `shutdown`/`restart`/`sleep`/`hibernate`/`lock` → shell command |
| `resolveOnCompleteCommand(spec, aliases)` | Resolves a `--on-complete` value through aliases → built-ins → literal |
| `runOnComplete(spec, aliases, {taskId, url, savePath, status})` | Runs the resolved, template-filled command |
| `sendNotification(String title, String body)` | Fires a platform desktop notification |

## Service install (`src/service_install.dart`)

| Function | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `installDaemonService()` | `Future<ServiceInstallResult>` — installs the platform auto-start entry (systemd/launchd/schtasks) |
| `uninstallDaemonService()` | `Future<ServiceInstallResult>` — removes it |

`ServiceInstallResult` is `{bool success, String message}`.

## History (`src/history.dart`)

| Member | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `HistoryLog({String? path})` | Defaults to `<state dir>/history.jsonl` |
| `.append(HistoryEntry entry)` | Appends one line |
| `.load({int? limit})` | Reads and parses all entries, newest first |
| `.clear()` | Deletes the log file |

`HistoryEntry` fields: `id`, `url`, `savePath`, `status`, `downloadedBytes`,
`durationMs`, `finishedAt`; computed getter `averageBytesPerSec`.

## Version (`src/version.dart`)

`String pdmVersion()` — returns the compiled-in version (via
`String.fromEnvironment('PDM_VERSION')`), falling back to reading
`pubspec.yaml` next to `Platform.script` under `dart run`, and finally to a
hardcoded fallback string.

# Changelog

## 3.1.0

- Added: `pause`, `resume`, `cancel`, `remove`, and `watch` now accept more
  than one id (`pdm remove id1 id2 id3`), with a batch confirmation prompt
  and a per-id success/failure summary. `add` now accepts more than one URL
  directly on the command line (`pdm add url1 url2`) in addition to
  `--file`.
- Added: much smarter, richer shell completion (`pdm completion
  bash|zsh`). It's generated straight from pdm's own flag definitions
  instead of a static word list, so it can't drift out of sync — see [Shell
  Completion](/pdm/shell-completion/) for the full behavior.
- Added: `uninstall` now actually removes everything pdm installed, not
  just the binaries — stops a running daemon, removes the auto-start
  service, deletes both bash and zsh completion scripts, and deletes config
  and download state/history. `--keep-config` keeps the config and
  history. Checks both system and per-user install locations regardless of
  the original `--user` choice.
- Added: `pdm help <command>` now lists a command's sub-actions (e.g.
  `daemon start|stop|...`) and, for flags with a fixed set of legal values,
  shows them inline.
- Added: an unrecognized `--flag` now suggests the closest known flag name,
  the same way unknown commands already do.
- Fixed: `--output` combined with `--file` (batch add) silently ignored
  `--output`; it's now a clear error instead.
- Fixed: `pdm watch <id>` and `pdm add <url>` (foreground mode) could hang
  forever if the daemon connection dropped mid-download — the event-stream
  listeners had no `onDone`/`onError` handling. Both now exit cleanly with
  an error message when the connection is lost.
- Fixed: `printTaskTable`/`pdm history` extracted the filename from a save
  path by splitting on `/` only, so a Windows path (`C:\\...\\file`)
  would display in full instead of just the filename. Both now share a
  single `basename()` helper that normalizes both separators.
- Fixed: `pdm pause <id>` / `pdm cancel <id>` could deadlock the daemon
  under a specific race between a segment cancel and the speed limiter's
  wait. Also fixed a `ConcurrentModificationError` risk from iterating the
  subscription list while a segment could concurrently remove from it.
- Fixed: `pdm daemon enable` and background auto-spawn silently failing
  once installed as a compiled binary, because daemon-path resolution
  depended on `Platform.script`, meaningless in a compiled executable. Now
  resolves `pdmd`/`pdmd.exe` as a sibling of the running `pdm` binary, with
  a `PDMD_PATH` override.
- Fixed: `pdmd` not shutting down cleanly on `SIGTERM` (the server handle
  was discarded, so `stop()` was never called and the unix socket was never
  released).
- Fixed: `pdm version` always printing the hardcoded fallback version after
  install, because it tried to read a `pubspec.yaml` that doesn't exist
  next to a compiled binary. Version is now baked in at compile time
  (`--define=PDM_VERSION=...`), with the old pubspec lookup kept only for
  `dart run` during development.
- Fixed: `pdm help <command>` (and `pdm <command> --help`) silently falling
  through to "Unknown command" for a bad command or a typo, instead of
  useful help; it now suggests the closest known command.
- Fixed: a bad/unknown flag combined with `--help` produced a parse error
  instead of showing help; `-h`/`--help` is now checked before strict flag
  parsing.
- Fixed: an unrecognized command previously still built a full CLI context
  (config load, daemon client setup) before reporting "Unknown command"; it
  now fails fast.
- Added: `pdm completion bash|zsh` now installs the script directly into
  the system completion directory instead of only printing it. On a
  permission error it prints the exact `sudo` command to re-run, plus a
  `--user` flag to install into the per-user completion dirs instead, and
  `--print` to keep the old print-to-stdout behavior.
- Added: the installer now installs to `/usr/bin` by default on Linux
  (previously always `~/.local/bin`, regardless of privilege). On a
  permission error it prints the exact `sudo` command to re-run, and a
  `--user` flag installs to `~/.local/bin` as before.
- Added: `<installer> uninstall` (and `<installer> uninstall --user`),
  which removes the installed binaries, the systemd `--user` service, and
  any completion scripts the installer or `pdm completion` placed.
- Added: the installer verifies a SHA-256 checksum of its embedded `pdm`/
  `pdmd` payloads before writing them to disk.
- Changed: the release workflow now runs on version tags (`v*.*.*`) instead
  of every push, and is gated behind `dart analyze`, `dart format
  --set-exit-if-changed`, and `dart test`. It also verifies the tag matches
  `pubspec.yaml` and publishes a `SHA256SUMS` file alongside the release
  binaries.
- Added: a `test/` suite covering the flag parser, help/unknown-command
  resolution, byte-size/duration parsing, checksum hashing, model JSON
  round-trips, and config loading.

## 2.0.0

Major rewrite. Highlights:

- Fixed: HTTP redirects, resumed downloads no longer truncate existing
  bytes, a queue-priority field that actually affects scheduling order,
  Windows-safe home directory / config / socket / state paths, and a
  handful of other latent bugs from the 2.0.0 rewrite itself.
- Added scheduling: `--at` (absolute or relative time), `--every`
  (recurring downloads), `--on-startup` (deferred until the daemon next
  starts).
- Added on-complete hooks (`--on-complete`) with cross-platform built-ins
  (shutdown, restart, sleep, hibernate, lock) plus user-defined aliases in
  the config file.
- Added regex-based download rules in the config file: per-URL-pattern
  overrides for save directory, connections, proxy, speed limit, headers,
  and on-complete hook.
- Added proxy authentication (`--proxy-user`/`--proxy-pass`) and a
  no-proxy bypass list.
- Added a global speed limit shared across all concurrent downloads,
  separate from each download's own `--speed-limit`.
- Added batch import: `pdm add --file urls.txt`.
- Added duplicate detection (same URL or save path); `--allow-duplicate` to
  override.
- Added disk-space checking before a download starts.
- Added exponential backoff between retries (`--linear-retries` to
  disable).
- Added desktop notifications on completion/failure (`notifications` in
  config).
- Added `pdm history` for a persistent log of completed/failed downloads.
- Added `pdm completion bash|zsh` for shell completion scripts.
- Added `pdm daemon enable`/`disable` to auto-start the daemon at login
  (systemd user service on Linux, scheduled task on Windows, launchd agent
  on macOS).
- Queued and startup-scheduled downloads now resume automatically when the
  daemon restarts, instead of sitting idle until manually resumed.
- Multi-connection downloads can now run in the background via a detached
  daemon (`pdmd`), reachable over a Unix socket (Linux) or TCP loopback
  (Windows); foreground mode remains available via `--foreground`.
- Added 20+ flags across every command: retries, speed limiting, checksum
  verification (MD5/SHA-1/SHA-256/SHA-512, pure-Dart, no crypto
  dependency), proxy, custom headers, cookies (inline or Netscape
  cookie-file), basic auth, TLS-insecure mode, redirect limits, queue
  priority, and more.
- Added a config file (YAML/TOML/JSON via `pdata`), resolved from
  `PDM_CONFIG_PATH` or `~/.config/pdm/pdm.yaml`. New `pdm config dump`
  command.
- Added output theming: `default`, `rainbow`, `catppuccin`.
- Split the codebase into a strict library/CLI boundary: `lib/src/*.dart`
  has no CLI awareness; `lib/src/cli/*.dart` owns flags and formatting.
- Merged `tool/generate_payload.dart` and `tool/installer.dart` into a
  single `tool/installer.dart` with `generate` and `install` modes.
- Removed `tool/print_version.dart`; version is read from `pubspec.yaml`
  directly (via `pdata` at runtime, via `sed` in the release workflow).
- Release workflow now publishes `pdm-linux-x64.exe` and
  `pdm-windows-x64.exe`, each a self-contained installer with both `pdm`

# License and Contributing

## License

See the [`LICENSE`](https://github.com/psdkjoon/pdm/blob/main/LICENSE) file
in the repository root for the full text.

## Repository

- Source: [github.com/psdkjoon/pdm](https://github.com/psdkjoon/pdm)
- Issues: [github.com/psdkjoon/pdm/issues](https://github.com/psdkjoon/pdm/issues)
- Releases: [github.com/psdkjoon/pdm/releases](https://github.com/psdkjoon/pdm/releases)

## Project layout

```text
pdm/
├── bin/
│   ├── pdm.dart          # CLI entrypoint
│   └── pdmd.dart         # daemon entrypoint
├── lib/
│   ├── pdm.dart          # public library exports
│   └── src/
│       ├── cli/          # flags, parsing, help text, output rendering — CLI-only
│       │   └── commands/ # one file per command (add, list, watch, ...)
│       ├── daemon/       # daemon protocol, client, server, socket address resolution
│       └── *.dart        # core engine: config, models, download_manager,
│                          # download_task, hashing, cookies, diskspace,
│                          # history, hooks, service_install, store, version
├── tool/
│   └── installer.dart    # generates/embeds the self-contained release installer
├── pubspec.yaml
└── CHANGELOG.md
```

The library/CLI split is deliberate and enforced by convention: `lib/src/*.dart`
(everything outside `cli/`) has zero awareness of flags, ANSI color, or
terminal output, which is what makes [using pdm as a plain Dart
library](/pdm/using-pdm-as-a-dart-library/) possible without dragging in CLI
concerns.

## Building and testing from source

```bash
git clone https://github.com/psdkjoon/pdm.git
cd pdm
dart pub get
dart analyze
dart format --set-exit-if-changed .
dart test
```

The release workflow (`.github/workflows/release.yml`) runs on version tags
(`v*.*.*`) and is gated behind exactly these three checks, plus a check that
the tag matches the `version` field in `pubspec.yaml`. It then compiles both
`pdm` and `pdmd` for each target platform, feeds them into
`tool/installer.dart generate` to embed both binaries and their SHA-256
checksums into a single self-contained installer, and publishes the
resulting `pdm-linux-x64.exe` / `pdm-windows-x64.exe` alongside a
`SHA256SUMS` file.

## Reporting issues

Please include your `pdm version` output, your OS/distro (e.g. "Arch
Linux"), and — for daemon-related issues — the output of `pdm daemon
status` when filing an issue.

## Dependencies

pdm intentionally keeps its dependency surface minimal: the only
third-party package is [`pdata`](https://pub.dev/packages/pdata) for config
serialization. Checksum hashing, HTTP, and CLI argument parsing are all
implemented directly against the Dart SDK — see [Using pdm as a Dart
Library](/pdm/using-pdm-as-a-dart-library/#checksums-srchashingdart) for
why that matters if you're depending on pdm's hashing functions elsewhere.

# pdm 2.0.0

This page documents pdm **2.0.0**, kept for historical reference. It was a
complete rewrite from 1.0.0 — the daemon, config file, scheduling, rules,
checksums, proxies, cookies, and themes all landed in this one release. If
you're setting up pdm today, use the [current version](/pdm/) instead,
which adds multi-id/multi-URL support, smarter shell completion, and a more
capable installer on top of everything below.

`pdm` is psdk's download manager: a multi-connection downloader with a
background daemon so transfers survive closing the terminal, resumable
downloads, scheduling, per-URL rules, and shell completion.

## Why a daemon?

Downloads started with `pdm add` run through a small background process,
`pdmd`, reachable over a Unix domain socket on Linux/macOS or a TCP
loopback socket on Windows — this is new at 2.0.0; 1.0.0 had no daemon and
`add` always blocked in the current process. Closing the terminal no longer
interrupts a transfer, and multiple `pdm` invocations share the same task
list.

Pass `--foreground`/`-f` to `pdm add` to block in the current terminal
instead, with no daemon involved — the same behavior `add` always had at
1.0.0.

## Install

```bash
dart pub global activate pdm
```

Or grab a self-contained installer from the [releases
page](https://github.com/psdkjoon/pdm/releases/latest): `pdm-linux-x64` and
`pdm-windows-x64.exe`, each embedding both `pdm` and the new `pdmd` daemon
binary. The installer always installs to `~/.local/bin` on Linux/macOS
(there's no `--user`/system-wide split or SHA-256 payload verification
yet — both arrive in 3.1.0) or `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\pdm` on Windows,
and adds that directory to `PATH` automatically where it can. There's no
`uninstall` subcommand at this version.

### Shell completion

```bash
pdm completion bash
pdm completion zsh
```

At 2.0.0 this only **prints** a static completion script to stdout for you
to redirect/source yourself — there's no `$SHELL` auto-detection (an
argument is required), no automatic install step, and no `--print`/`--user`
flags (those, along with permission-aware install and value-aware
completions, arrive in 3.1.0).

## Core concepts

- **Task** — one download, identified by an id assigned when you `pdm add`
  it (8 characters, up from 6 at 1.0.0).
- **Segment** — a byte range of a task's file, same model as 1.0.0.
- **Daemon (`pdmd`)** — new at this version. `pdm` is now a thin client
  that talks to it over a socket, except in `--foreground` mode.
- **Rule** — new at this version. A regex-based override in the config
  file that changes options for URLs matching a pattern.
- **Schedule** — new at this version. A task can start at a specific time
  (`--at`), repeat on an interval (`--every`), or wait for the next daemon
  startup (`--on-startup`).

## First download

```bash
pdm add https://example.com/big-file.iso
```

Queues the download with the daemon (auto-spawning it if needed) and
returns immediately — the default flips from 1.0.0's always-blocking
behavior. Use `pdm watch <id>` to follow along, or add `-f`/`--foreground`
to block with a progress bar in the current process like 1.0.0 always did.

`pdm add` still only accepts **one URL** per invocation directly on the
command line at this version (multi-URL support arrives in 3.1.0) — for
multiple downloads at once, use `--file urls.txt`, which is itself new at
2.0.0.

## As a library

```dart
import 'package:pdm/pdm.dart';

final manager = DownloadManager();
manager.add(
  'https://example.com/file.iso',
  options: const TaskOptions(connections: 8, retries: 5),
  schedule: Schedule(every: Duration(days: 1)),
);
```

`lib/src/*.dart` still has no CLI awareness, same split as 1.0.0 — only now
there's a `lib/src/cli/` and `lib/src/daemon/` to be split *from*.

# Configuration (2.0.0)

New at this version — 1.0.0 had no config file at all. Behavior described
here carries forward essentially unchanged into 3.1.0; the config file
format and every key below is identical between 2.0.0 and the [current
version](/pdm/configuration/).

## File location

| Source | Path |
| --- | --- |
| Default (Linux/macOS) | `~/.config/pdm/pdm.yaml` |
| Default (Windows) | `%APPDATA%\pdm\pdm.yaml` |
| Override | `$PDM_CONFIG_PATH` environment variable |
| Per-command override | `--config <path>` / `-g <path>` |

Format inferred from extension (`.yaml`/`.yml`, `.toml`, `.json`) via
[`pdata`](https://pub.dev/packages/pdata) — the one and only third-party
dependency pdm gained at this rewrite (1.0.0 had zero).

```bash
pdm config dump --output ~/.config/pdm/pdm.yaml
pdm config dump --format toml --output ~/.config/pdm/pdm.toml
pdm config dump
```

## Full key reference

Every key below already exists at 2.0.0 with the same name, type, and
default it has in the [current version](/pdm/configuration-schema/):
`connections`, `maxConcurrentTasks`, `retries`, `retryDelay`,
`retryBackoff`, `timeout`, `speedLimit`, `globalSpeedLimit`,
`maxRedirects`, `insecure`, `downloadDir`, `theme`, `color`, `daemonHost`,
`daemonPort`, `socketPath`, `proxy`, `proxyUser`, `proxyPass`,
`proxyBypass`, `onCompleteAliases`, `rules`, `notifications`,
`checkDiskSpace`.

## Per-URL rules

Also unchanged from 2.0.0 onward — `pattern` (required, regex), `saveDir`
(or legacy alias `dir`), `connections`, `proxy`, `speedLimit`, `headers`,
`onComplete`, first match wins, checked top to bottom:

```yaml
rules:
  - pattern: "example\\.com/videos/"
    saveDir: "~/Videos"
    connections: 16
  - pattern: "\\.iso$"
    saveDir: "~/ISOs"
    proxy: "http://127.0.0.1:8080"
```

## Precedence

Flag > matching rule > config file > built-in default — same order used at
every version since the config file was introduced.

# Environment Variables (2.0.0)

New at this version: `PDM_CONFIG_PATH`, `XDG_STATE_HOME` (state directory
already existed conceptually at 1.0.0, since a state file was always
written to `$XDG_STATE_HOME/pdm`, but now also underlies the daemon socket
path), and the Windows equivalents (`APPDATA`, `LOCALAPPDATA`,
`USERPROFILE`).

`PDMD_PATH` does **not** exist yet at 2.0.0 — daemon binary discovery at
this version relies on `Platform.script`, which only resolves correctly
under `dart run` and breaks for a compiled, installed binary. This is a
known rough edge fixed in 3.1.0 (see the [current
docs](/pdm/environment-variables/) and the
[changelog](/pdm/changelog/#3.1.0)); at 2.0.0, `pdm daemon enable` and
background auto-spawn from an installed binary can fail to locate `pdmd`
with no override available.

# Guides (2.0.0)

Guided walkthroughs for pdm 2.0.0. The content on these pages matches the
[current version's guides](/pdm/guides/) almost exactly, since nearly the
entire feature set (scheduling, hooks, rules, checksums, proxies, themes,
resume behavior) was introduced whole in this release and hasn't changed
since. The differences worth knowing about, all UX polish added later in
3.1.0:

- `add`, `pause`, `resume`, `cancel`, `remove`, and `watch` each take
  **exactly one** URL/id — no multiple positionals, no bulk `--all` on
  `pause`/`resume`/`cancel`/`remove` beyond what's listed below, and no
  confirmation-prompt batching.
- `pdm completion` only prints a script; it doesn't install one.
- Command help (`pdm help <command>`) doesn't list sub-actions or inline
  flag choices, and unknown commands/flags don't get "did you mean"
  suggestions.

See [Configuration](/pdm/configuration/) (2.0.0 version) for the full
config file and per-URL rules reference, which is unchanged going forward.

## Adding downloads

```bash
pdm add https://example.com/file.iso
pdm add https://example.com/file.iso --output ~/ISOs/custom-name.iso
pdm add https://example.com/file.iso --foreground
pdm add --file urls.txt
```

All the per-task flags exist already at 2.0.0: headers (`--header`,
repeatable), `--user-agent`, `--referer`, cookies (`--cookie`/
`--cookie-file`), proxy + proxy auth, retries/backoff, timeout, speed
limit, checksum verification, basic auth, `--insecure`, `--overwrite`,
`--start-paused`, `--priority`, `--max-redirects`, scheduling flags, and
`--on-complete`. See [Commands: add](/pdm/commands-add/) (current version)
for the full flag table — it's identical at 2.0.0 except for the
multi-URL-on-command-line capability, which didn't exist yet (only
`--file` could add more than one URL per invocation).

Duplicate detection (same url/save path) and `--allow-duplicate` already
work the same way as the current version.

## Multi-connection downloads and resume

Segmentation, resume-by-exact-byte-range, checksum verification
(`md5`/`sha1`/`sha256`/`sha512`, pure Dart), disk-space checking, and
per-task/global speed limiting are all already present, unchanged, at
2.0.0. See [Multi-Connection Downloads &
Resume](/pdm/multi-connection-downloads-and-resume/) (current version) for
the full explanation.

## Scheduling

`--at` (ISO date/time, `HH:mm`, or `+<duration>`), `--every` (recurring),
and `--on-startup` are all present and work exactly as in the [current
version](/pdm/scheduling/).

## On-complete hooks

The five built-ins (`shutdown`, `restart`, `sleep`, `hibernate`, `lock`),
custom `onCompleteAliases`, and `{id}`/`{url}`/`{path}`/`{status}`
substitution are all present and unchanged. See [On-Complete
Hooks](/pdm/on-complete-hooks/) (current version).

## Managing tasks

```bash
pdm list
pdm ls
pdm pause <id>
pdm resume <id>
pdm cancel <id>
pdm remove <id> [--delete-file]
pdm watch <id>
```

Every one of `pause`/`resume`/`cancel`/`remove` takes **a single id**
(`--all`/`-A` already exists and selects the same status sets described in
the [current guide](/pdm/managing-tasks/#bulk-operations-with---all), but
explicit multi-id lists like `pdm remove id1 id2 id3` are **not**
supported — that's a 3.1.0 addition). `cancel`/`remove` already prompt for
confirmation unless `--force`/`-F` is passed or `stdin` isn't a terminal.

`pdm watch` also takes a single id only — watching several ids at once in
one invocation arrives in 3.1.0.

## Daemon & service

```bash
pdm daemon start
pdm daemon stop
pdm daemon status
pdm daemon enable
pdm daemon disable
```

All present and working the same way as the [current
version](/pdm/daemon-and-service/) — systemd user service on Linux, launchd
agent on macOS, Scheduled Task on Windows.

## Themes

`default`, `rainbow`, and `catppuccin` all already exist at 2.0.0, selected
via `--theme`/`-T` or the config file's `theme` key, exactly as in the
[current version](/pdm/themes/).

## Proxies & networking

`--proxy`, `--proxy-user`/`--proxy-pass`, `proxyBypass`, `--insecure`,
`--max-redirects`, `--timeout` all already exist, unchanged.

# CLI Overview (2.0.0)

```
pdm <command> [flags]
```

## Global flags

| Short | Long | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-v` | `--verbose` | Print extra diagnostic output |
| `-q` | `--quiet` | Suppress non-essential output |
| `-j` | `--json` | Machine-readable JSON output |
| `-H` | `--daemon-host` | Daemon TCP host (Windows only) |
| `-P` | `--daemon-port` | Daemon TCP port (Windows only) |
| `-s` | `--socket-path` | Daemon Unix socket path (Linux/macOS only) |
| `-n` | `--no-spawn` | Fail instead of auto-spawning the daemon |
| `-g` | `--config` | Path to config file |
| `-T` | `--theme` | `default`, `rainbow`, or `catppuccin` |
| `-N` | `--no-color` | Disable ANSI colors |
| `-h` | `--help` | Show help for this command |

Every one of these already exists at 2.0.0, identical to the [current
version](/pdm/cli-overview/) — the entire global-flag surface was
introduced whole in this release (1.0.0 had none of it).

## Commands

`add`, `list`/`ls`, `pause`, `resume`/`start`, `cancel`, `remove`/`rm`,
`watch`, `daemon`, `config`, `history`, `completion`, `version`, `help` —
the same 13-command surface as the current version. The commands
themselves, their aliases, and their flags are essentially all present
already; what's missing is UX polish layered on in 3.1.0:

- `pdm help <command>` prints a flat flag list only — no sub-action
  listing (e.g. `daemon start|stop|...`), no inline `(one of: ...)` choice
  hints on flags with a fixed value set.
- An unknown command just says `Unknown command "x". Run "pdm help" for a
  list of commands.` — no closest-match suggestion.
- An unrecognized `--flag` is a plain parse error — no "did you mean"
  suggestion either.
- `-h`/`--help` combined with an otherwise-invalid flag on the same command
  line produces a parse error instead of showing help (fixed in 3.1.0 by
  checking for `--help` before strict parsing).

## Flag precedence

Same order as the current version: flag > matching rule > config file >
built-in default.

# Changelog (as of 2.0.0)

## 2.0.0

Major rewrite. Highlights:

- Fixed: HTTP redirects, resumed downloads no longer truncate existing
  bytes, a queue-priority field that actually affects scheduling order,
  Windows-safe home directory / config / socket / state paths, and a
  handful of other latent bugs from the 2.0.0 rewrite itself.
- Added scheduling: `--at` (absolute or relative time), `--every`
  (recurring downloads), `--on-startup` (deferred until the daemon next
  starts).
- Added on-complete hooks (`--on-complete`) with cross-platform built-ins
  (shutdown, restart, sleep, hibernate, lock) plus user-defined aliases in
  the config file.
- Added regex-based download rules in the config file: per-URL-pattern
  overrides for save directory, connections, proxy, speed limit, headers,
  and on-complete hook.
- Added proxy authentication (`--proxy-user`/`--proxy-pass`) and a
  no-proxy bypass list.
- Added a global speed limit shared across all concurrent downloads,
  separate from each download's own `--speed-limit`.
- Added batch import: `pdm add --file urls.txt`.
- Added duplicate detection (same URL or save path); `--allow-duplicate` to
  override.
- Added disk-space checking before a download starts.
- Added exponential backoff between retries (`--linear-retries` to
  disable).
- Added desktop notifications on completion/failure (`notifications` in
  config).
- Added `pdm history` for a persistent log of completed/failed downloads.
- Added `pdm completion bash|zsh` for shell completion scripts.
- Added `pdm daemon enable`/`disable` to auto-start the daemon at login
  (systemd user service on Linux, scheduled task on Windows, launchd agent
  on macOS).
- Queued and startup-scheduled downloads now resume automatically when the
  daemon restarts, instead of sitting idle until manually resumed.
- Multi-connection downloads can now run in the background via a detached
  daemon (`pdmd`), reachable over a Unix socket (Linux) or TCP loopback
  (Windows); foreground mode remains available via `--foreground`.
- Added 20+ flags across every command: retries, speed limiting, checksum
  verification (MD5/SHA-1/SHA-256/SHA-512, pure-Dart, no crypto
  dependency), proxy, custom headers, cookies (inline or Netscape
  cookie-file), basic auth, TLS-insecure mode, redirect limits, queue
  priority, and more.
- Added a config file (YAML/TOML/JSON via `pdata`), resolved from
  `PDM_CONFIG_PATH` or `~/.config/pdm/pdm.yaml`. New `pdm config dump`
  command.
- Added output theming: `default`, `rainbow`, `catppuccin`.
- Split the codebase into a strict library/CLI boundary: `lib/src/*.dart`
  has no CLI awareness; `lib/src/cli/*.dart` owns flags and formatting.
- Merged `tool/generate_payload.dart` and `tool/installer.dart` into a
  single `tool/installer.dart` with `generate` and `install` modes.
- Removed `tool/print_version.dart`; version is read from `pubspec.yaml`
  directly (via `pdata` at runtime, via `sed` in the release workflow).
- Release workflow now publishes `pdm-linux-x64.exe` and
  `pdm-windows-x64.exe`, each a self-contained installer with both `pdm`
  and `pdmd` embedded.

# pdm 1.0.0

This page documents pdm's **first release**, kept for historical reference.
If you're setting up pdm today, use the [current version](/pdm/) instead —
almost everything described here (the daemon, config file, scheduling,
rules, checksums, and every flag beyond `-o`/`-c`/`--delete-file`) did not
exist yet at 1.0.0.

`pdm` 1.0.0 is psdk's download manager: a minimal, dependency-free,
multi-connection downloader — library and CLI in one package, no daemon, no
config file, no third-party Dart dependency at all.

## Install

```bash
dart pub global activate pdm
```

Or grab a self-contained installer (no internet needed at install time)
from the [releases page](https://github.com/psdk/pdm/releases/latest). The
installer always installs to `~/.local/bin` on Linux/macOS (there's no
`--user`/system-wide split yet) or `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\pdm` on
Windows, and adds that directory to `PATH` if it can (printing the export
line for you to add manually on Linux/macOS if it can't do so
automatically).

There is no `pdm uninstall` command at this version — remove the installed
binary and, if you added one, your `PATH` export line, by hand.

## Usage

```bash
pdm add <url> [-o <output-path>] [-c <connections>]
pdm list
pdm pause <id>
pdm resume <id>
pdm watch <id>
pdm cancel <id>
pdm remove <id> [--delete-file]
pdm help
pdm --version
```

`pdm add` runs synchronously in the current process and blocks with a live
progress bar until the download finishes, fails, or is canceled — there is
no background/daemon mode yet, so `--foreground`/`--background` don't
exist because there's nothing to choose between.

## Core concepts, as they exist at 1.0.0

- **Task** — one download, identified by a **6-character** lowercase
  alphanumeric id (later versions use 8 characters).
- **Segment** — same idea as later versions: a byte-range slice, up to
  `-c`/`--connections` of them, downloaded concurrently and written
  directly into the destination file at the right offset. The `connections`
  count is clamped to 1–32.
- No daemon, no rules, no scheduling — a task exists only in the current
  process's memory plus its on-disk state file; there's nothing external to
  connect to.

## State file

Task state is persisted as JSON at `$XDG_STATE_HOME/pdm/state.json`,
falling back to `~/.local/state/pdm/state.json` if `XDG_STATE_HOME` isn't
set. There is no config file at all at this version — nothing to point at
via `PDM_CONFIG_PATH`, since that variable doesn't exist yet either.

## Save location

Downloads save to `$HOME/Downloads/<inferred-name>` by default (no `~`
expansion logic — it reads `$HOME` directly), or to the path given via
`-o`/`--output`. There's no `downloadDir` config key to change the default,
since there's no config file.

# Commands & Flags (1.0.0)

The complete command and flag surface of pdm 1.0.0 — far smaller than
later versions. Every flag shown here is the *entire* flag set that exists
at this version; there's no shared "global flags" concept yet (no
`--json`, `--verbose`, `--config`, `--theme`, `--no-color`, etc. — none of
that exists until the 2.0.0 rewrite).

## `pdm add`

```
pdm add <url> [-o <output-path>] [-c <connections>]
```

| Short | Long | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-o` | `--output` | Save path for the downloaded file |
| `-c` | `--connections` | Number of concurrent connections/segments |

Takes exactly one URL (no multi-URL, no `--file` batch mode). Always runs
in the foreground with a live progress bar; always starts immediately
(there's no `--start-paused`, no scheduling flags of any kind). No headers,
cookies, auth, proxy, retries, checksum, or speed-limit flags exist yet.

## `pdm list` (alias: `ls`)

```
pdm list
```

No flags — always prints every task in creation order, one line per task
plus its save path on the following line. No `--status`/`--sort`/`--json`.

## `pdm pause <id>`

```
pdm pause <id>
```

No flags, single id only.

## `pdm resume <id>` (alias: `start`)

```
pdm resume <id>
```

No flags, single id only.

## `pdm cancel <id>`

```
pdm cancel <id>
```

No flags, single id only. No confirmation prompt — cancels immediately.

## `pdm remove <id>` (alias: `rm`)

```
pdm remove <id> [--delete-file]
```

| Long | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--delete-file` | Also delete the downloaded file |

No short form for `--delete-file` yet. No confirmation prompt. Single id
only.

## `pdm watch <id>`

```
pdm watch <id>
```

No flags. Starts the task if it isn't already running, then prints a
live progress line until it reaches a terminal state. No `--interval`,
no `--no-bar` — the display is always the same fixed-width bar.

## `pdm help` / `pdm -h` / `pdm --help`

Prints the fixed usage text shown under [Getting
Started](/pdm/getting-started/#usage). No `pdm help <command>` — help is
one static block covering every command at once.

## `pdm version` / `pdm -v` / `pdm --version`

Prints `pdm <version>`. `pdmVersion()` reads the `version` field from the
nearest `pubspec.yaml` above the running script (walking up to 6 parent
directories), falling back to the literal string `"unknown"` if that fails
— there's no `--define=PDM_VERSION=...` bake-in mechanism yet, so a
compiled 1.0.0 binary run outside its source tree reports `unknown`.

## What doesn't exist yet

For readers coming from the current docs, here's what 1.0.0 has **no**
equivalent of at all: the daemon (`pdmd`, `pdm daemon ...`), the config
file and every flag that falls back to it, `pdm config`, `pdm history`,
`pdm completion`, scheduling (`--at`/`--every`/`--on-startup`),
`--on-complete` hooks, checksums, proxies, cookies, custom headers, basic
auth, speed limiting, retries/backoff, disk space checks, duplicate
detection, themes, `--json` output, and multi-id/multi-URL support on any
command.

# Task Lifecycle (1.0.0)

A much smaller status set than later versions — no `scheduled` status
(nothing schedules anything yet) and `merging` is declared in the code but
never actually reached in practice, since segments are already written
directly to their final offsets with no separate merge pass.

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `queued` | Just added, not yet started |
| `probing` | Checking size/range support before starting segments |
| `downloading` | Actively transferring |
| `paused` | Stopped by `pdm pause`; segment progress preserved |
| `merging` | Declared in the code for forward-compatibility; not used by any transition in 1.0.0 |
| `completed` | Finished successfully — **no checksum verification exists**, so this is the only success state |
| `failed` | A segment errored out, or the download finished with incomplete segments |
| `canceled` | Stopped by `pdm cancel` or `pdm remove`; partial file deleted |

## Resume behavior

Identical in spirit to later versions: each segment's `downloaded` byte
count is persisted, and resuming asks the server only for the remaining
range (`Range: bytes=<start+downloaded>-<end>`). There's no retry loop at
this version, though — if a segment's request throws, its error is
recorded and the task simply ends up `failed` once every segment settles;
there's no `--retries`/`--retry-delay`/backoff to smooth over transient
failures.

## On process restart

Since there's no daemon, "restart" here means re-running `dart pub global
activate`'d `pdm` (or the installed binary) with a fresh process. On
`DownloadManager` construction, any task that was `downloading` or
`probing` when the state file was last written is moved to `paused` — the
same one-time correction later versions still perform on daemon startup,
just triggered by process start instead of daemon start.
